title: Models and data
summary: Review model artifacts, training inputs, and dependency provenance.
html:
Objectives

  • Inventory artifacts and the identities permitted to change them.
  • Distinguish poisoning, extraction, and membership inference.
  • Design controlled experiments using synthetic data.

Concepts and boundaries

AI supply chains include datasets, pretrained weights, adapters, tokenizers, packages, build steps, and serving images. A model file is an input to software and may invoke a loader with substantial privileges. An assessment should identify the format and loading behavior before opening an unfamiliar artifact.

Data poisoning changes a dataset or training pipeline to influence behavior. Model extraction attempts to approximate a model through observations, while membership inference asks whether particular data contributed to training. These are different hypotheses and require different evaluation designs. A single familiar-looking answer does not establish training-data membership.

Open full-size diagram

Practice checklist

Use an isolated lab or an explicitly authorized environment. Record prerequisites and configuration before changing inputs.

  1. Choose a small local sample project and inventory model files, dependency lockfiles, datasets, and source revisions.
  2. Record artifact hashes and expected download origins without executing untrusted loaders.
  3. Review configuration for automatic remote code execution or unsafe deserialization; document the exact setting and loading path.
  4. For a disposable training example, compare a clean synthetic dataset against a deliberately altered copy using a held-out evaluation set.
  5. Record the change, sample size, measurement method, and limitations; distinguish correlation from evidence of the proposed cause.

Expected observations

An inventory should establish what runs, where it came from, and how it is verified. A controlled behavioral difference supports a hypothesis about your experiment; it does not demonstrate a vulnerability in an unrelated hosted model.

Mitigations and retesting

Pin and verify artifacts, isolate loading/build environments, review dependency changes, limit training-data write access, and evaluate behavior before promoting new models. Avoid treating file extensions or repository popularity as proof of safety.
